newsitem.title: INDIA: Finland urges India to open up banking, insurance.
newsitem.headline: Finland urges India to open up banking, insurance.

text.p: Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari on Tuesday urged India to open its vast banking and insurance sectors to private industry, which businessmen said was a crucial step to boost its crumbling infrastructure.
Ahtisaari told a meeting of Indian businessmen that free market reforms introduced in 1991 had accelerated economic growth and strengthened the external aspects of India's economy.
But he said India must pay great attention to revamping its inadequate infrastructure if the growth was to continue.

"In order for this dynamic development to continue, there is now a need for the implementation of internal reforms in the direction of an open market economy also in sectors such as banking and insurance," Ahtisaari said.
Indian officials estimate the country must pour $200 billion into improving infrastructure over the next 10 years, the bulk of which will come from foreign private enterprise.

"Without energy there is no industrial production, without telecommunications no efficiently functioning economic life, without adequate harbours and transport capacity, exports and imports become bottlenecks in development," Ahtisaari said.
Ahtisaari is leading a delegation representing more than 25 large Finnish firms to India to seek business opportunities.

The delegation wants to especially increase cooperation between Indian and Finnish business in areas such as telecommunications, power generation and transmission, cargo handling and forestry, in which Finland has special expertise.
Many of these are precisely the skills India most needs to eliminate its infrastructure bottlenecks, Ahtisaari said.

Members of the delegation said funds for infrastructure development would flow in once India opened its banking and insurance sectors to foreign private enterprise. "You need a more open, independent financial market," said Georg Ehrnrooth, the chairman of the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT). "In today's international trade and business, one of the key questions is financing.

"The possibilities and needs (of infrastructure) are usually much bigger than the possibilities of finance. If you can open opportunities to the international finance and investment community, that will open opportunities to fund infrastructure," Ehrnrooth added.
Ahtisaari said India could pit its own strengths and competitive advantages against growing external challenges.

"Finland, despite its small size and paucity of capital, can prove an interesting cooperation partner for an India striving to raise the level of her industrial technology and boost her international competitiveness," he added.
